summary: DAY batch discovery reviewed all 12 Chief-selected active companies using cumulative primary evidence plus current-cycle source-health and fresh public signals. Company-level discovery coverage is sufficient for Chief adjudication on all 12; no company is blocked here solely by a global discovery defect. Global T0 discovery remains fail-closed because FINRA is only partition-fresh with eventDataAvailable=false and the standing cadence directive is still open, so acquisitionComplete is false at the lane-global level.

companies.finding: Fresh strategic/facility signals strengthen demand and infrastructure relevance: NVIDIA announced a $2B investment/partnership and Nebius says its Missouri AI factory can scale to 1.2 GW. These are demand/capacity signals, not proof of returns on capital; concentration and capex remain explicit.

Current filing evidence already captures concentrated government/commercial demand, RPO/backlog and financing lineage. No fresh signal found that invalidates treatment this cycle; absence of a new event is not a blocker.

Commercial frameworks and regulatory milestones remain the key weak-signal cluster. The Switch 12GW framework should be treated as optionality until individual binding agreements exist; licensing/fuel milestones are catalysts, not present revenue.

Q2 evidence confirms AI-infrastructure optionality exists alongside a still material self-mining business and financing dependence. Discovery should continue separating AI-customer wins from mining-driven economics rather than treating the narrative as one business.
unknowns: future AI colocation customer mix and conversion

companies.finding: Fresh September signal is material: IonQ launched Superion 256, says first integrated 256-qubit chips were fabricated at SkyWater, first ions trapped, and customer deliveries targeted for 2027. This reduces the manufacturing-integration uncertainty but does not prove commercial unit economics or fault-tolerant roadmap success.

No new external event overrides the primary concentration signal: Walmart-linked deployment dependence remains the central weak-signal risk, while large backlog/RPO remains demand evidence rather than diversification proof.

Current AI/custom-silicon/optical demand remains structurally relevant, but customer/distributor concentration is already high enough that new design wins should be tracked for diversification rather than counted only as growth.

AI datacenter optical demand remains the dominant positive signal. Existing customer concentration and leverage make supplier/customer diversification signals more decision-relevant than generic AI demand headlines.
AI optical demand and 1.6T/CPO transition remain the key signal cluster; debt-to-equity restructuring materially changed capital structure and must travel with any growth signal.

AI/server power-management demand is supported by strong current operating results, while distributor/geographic concentration keeps manufacturing-resilience and channel-end-customer mapping as the highest-value future signal set.

Hyperscaler/CCS growth is a meaningful structural signal but concentration is already explicit. Future signal collection should emphasize customer-mix broadening, margin durability and capex intensity rather than only revenue growth.

Broad end-market diversification remains a positive resilience signal. The 2026 acquisition program materially increases debt/integration importance, so future weak-signal monitoring should focus on integration slippage, leverage trajectory and cross-selling evidence.

materialFindings.globalSourceHealth: Automated required-source health is 4/4 and coverageRatio=1, but FINRA OTC Daily List remains observationMode=partition-freshness with eventDataAvailable=false. This is a capability gap, not row-level corporate-action acquisition. SAM.gov remains deferred by owner configuration. These global conditions remain separate from company-level readiness.

IONQ's manufacturing milestone reduces a roadmap uncertainty while acquisition dilution/cash use and commercial economics remain unresolved.
Large backlogs/frameworks at SYM and OKLO are not equivalent to diversified or binding economic value capture.
